        ### Question
        Certain glucose transporters that are expressed predominantly on skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes are unique compared to those transporters found on other cell types within the body. Without directly affecting glucose transport in other cell types, which of the following would be most likely to selectively increase glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes?

        ### Options
        opa. Increased levels of circulating insulin
opb. Decreased levels of circulating insulin
opc. Increased plasma glucose concentration
opd. Decreased plasma glucose concentration
ope. It is physiologically impossible to selectively increase glucose uptake in specific cells

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Increased levels of circulating insulin -> Activation of insulin receptors on skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes -> Increased translocation of glucose transporters (GLUT4) to the cell membrane -> Enhanced glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes -> Selective increase in glucose uptake in these cells -> 95%
CHAIN: Decreased levels of circulating insulin -> Reduced activation of insulin receptors on skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes -> Decreased translocation of glucose transporters (GLUT4) to the cell membrane -> Impaired glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes -> 90%

### Retrieved Evidence Paths (broad but correct):
(Adipocytes)-INTERACTS_WITH/LOCATION_OF->(Glucose Transporter)
(Glucose Transporter)-INTERACTS_WITH->(Adipocytes)
(Insulin Receptor)-INTERACTS_WITH->(Cells)-INTERACTS_WITH/LOCATION_OF->(Glucose Transporter)
